title: Shelf Loss Percentage Charged on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking Return
content:
The percentage charged is then fixed. Where the item was held longer than the schedule's return window and the grade recorded is that it came back opened with something missing from the box or damaged by the customer, the stale damaged fee percentage is charged. Where the item was held longer than the schedule's return window and the grade recorded is that it came back new and sealed or opened with everything in the box, the stale fee percentage is charged. Where the item was held longer than the schedule's return window divided by the short hold divisor but not longer than that window, the held fee percentage is charged. In any other case the schedule's own restocking percentage is charged.

The stale damaged fee percentage is 22. The stale fee percentage is 18. The held fee percentage is 14. The short hold divisor is 2.

## The window the holding is measured against

The percentage charged on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking return is measured against the return window published against the schedule the line falls under, and against half that window.

| Return schedule | Return window | That window divided by 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard Fifteen Day Return | 15 days | 7.5 days |
| Member Extended Thirty Day Return | 30 days | 15 days |
| Major Appliance Forty Eight Hour Return | 2 days | 1 day |
| Activated Wireless Device Return | 14 days | 7 days |
| Open Box and Clearance Final Sale | 0 days | 0 days |
| Business Contract Return Schedule | 45 days | 22.5 days |

The grade read is the condition last recorded by an inspection on the return.

## The ladder in full

| Days the item was held | Grade last recorded | Percentage charged |
| --- | --- | --- |
| longer than the schedule's return window | opened with something missing from the box, or damaged by the customer | 22 per cent |
| longer than the schedule's return window | new and sealed, or opened with everything in the box | 18 per cent |
| longer than half the schedule's return window but not longer than that window | any grade | 14 per cent |
| any other case, including a holding longer than the window on any other grade | — | the restocking percentage published against the schedule the line falls under |

## Both sides of the thresholds, on hypothetical inputs

*A schedule whose return window is 20 days, the item held 21 days, the grade last recorded being damaged by the customer.* Twenty-one is longer than 20, so 22 per cent is charged.

*The same schedule, the item held 21 days, the grade last recorded being new and sealed.* Twenty-one is longer than 20 on a grade in the second row, so 18 per cent is charged.

*The same schedule, the item held exactly 20 days.* Twenty is not longer than 20, but it is longer than 10, so 14 per cent is charged.

*The same schedule, the item held exactly 10 days.* Ten is not longer than 10, so the schedule's own restocking percentage is charged.

*The same schedule, the item held 21 days, the grade last recorded being beyond economic repair.* That grade appears in neither of the first two rows, and 21 days is longer than the window rather than inside it, so the case falls to the last row and the schedule's own restocking percentage is charged.
